title: Fishhawk grooming report artifact (plan-stage sibling)
description: The SECOND additive sibling of the plan artifact (after clarification-request-v1), produced by a `plan`-typed PROPOSE stage running the backlog_grooming workflow (ADR-065 §3, ADR-067 §2). Selected over plan-standard-v1 by the top-level 'kind' discriminator BEFORE validation, so plan-standard-v1.schema.json stays frozen. A grooming report is a PROPOSAL, never an applied mutation: it states a proposed ordering with per-item rubric-cited scores, duplicate candidates, hygiene defects, suggested depends_on edges, vision-drift flags, and decomposition suggestions, and a human decides what (if anything) to apply. THE LOAD-BEARING CONSTRAINT: an ordering entry MUST cite at least one charter rubric line (`rubric_citations` is required with minItems:1), so a ranking that cannot be justified against the charter is REJECTED by this schema rather than merely shipped undecorated — charter §5.1 states the rule, this schema enforces it. Every entry carries a stable `id` DERIVED from the underlying backlog item and proposal class (never minted per run), so two reports over the same backlog diff mechanically run-over-run (#2240). See grooming-report-v1.md for the normative id-derivation contract.

kind.description: Top-level discriminator. The plan package routes an artifact carrying this value to this schema; a clarification_request routes to clarification-request-v1 and anything else (carrying plan_version) to plan-standard-v1. This sibling intentionally omits plan_version so the artifacts never collide on a shared required field.

report_version.description: Artifact schema version, mirroring the plan artifact's plan_version. Single-value enum: a future breaking change bumps to grooming_report_v2 with its own schema file rather than editing this one in place.

summary.description: Human-readable lead paragraph: what backlog slice was groomed, over what window, and the headline of what the report proposes. Rendered first at the operator gate.

charter_ref.description: Optional in grooming_report_v1, INTENDED REQUIRED in the next major: the pinned charter the report was scored against. Left optional here because the charter resolution/injection machinery is E54.2 / #2234's slice and this artifact must not block on it. Draft 2020-12 §10.3 collects x-intended-required as an annotation, so declaring the intent here changes no validation result.

ordering.description: The proposed ranking, one entry per item, each citing at least one charter rubric line. Required and non-empty: a grooming report that proposes no ordering has nothing for the operator to decide. Ranks must be exactly the permutation 1..N (enforced semantically — JSON Schema cannot express it).

duplicates.description: Candidate duplicate/superseded PAIRS (charter S2). Required as an array — an empty array states 'none found', which is a different claim from omitting the key. Never destructive: the report flags the pair and its basis; a human decides.

hygiene_defects.description: Objective, reversible structural defects (charter S4). Required as an array; empty states 'none found'.

dependency_edges.description: Suggested depends_on edges between backlog items. DIRECTIONAL: from depends on to. Required as an array; empty states 'none found'.

vision_drift.description: Items advancing a charter non-goal (§3) or mis-aligned with a phase theme. Charter §5.3: drift is reported as a finding, never quietly ranked last. Required as an array; empty states 'none found'.

decomposition_suggestions.description: Items the groomer proposes splitting into children. Required as an array; empty states 'none found'.

ticket-reference.description: The ticket the grooming RUN was opened against (the run's originating issue), not an item being groomed. Shape mirrors plan-standard-v1 verbatim.

type.description: v0 closed set; v0.x adds linear_ticket and jira_ticket. Mirrors plan-standard-v1.

url.description: Canonical URL of the originating ticket.

agent.description: Agent identifier matching the workflow spec's executor.agent.

version.description: Optional. Model version or build SHA when agent reports it.

timestamp.description: RFC 3339 timestamp of generation. The runner wall-clock at agent invocation.

charter-ref.description: The exact charter revision the report was scored against, so a reviewer can reproduce the scoring and #2240 can tell a genuinely-changed ranking from one that moved because the charter did.

path.description: Repo-relative path of the charter document (e.g. ".fishhawk/charter.md").

content_hash.description: Hex-encoded SHA-256 of the charter bytes the report was scored against.

ref.description: Optional. Git ref or commit SHA the charter was read at.

item-ref.description: A reference to one backlog item. `type` is the PROVIDER DISCRIMINATOR and participates in the derived item-key — identical textual coordinates on two forges are DIFFERENT items and must not collide on one key (see grooming-report-v1.md § Entry-id derivation).

type.description: Provider discriminator. Each admitted value has a defined item-key derivation: github_issue → "github/<id>", gitlab_issue → "gitlab/<id>", jira_issue → "jira/<id>", each lowercased. Never widen this enum without adding the matching derivation case in plan.GroomingEntryID — a value the derivation cannot handle would make the entry id underivable.

id.description: Provider-native stable coordinates: "<owner>/<repo>#<number>" for github_issue, "<namespace>/<project>#<number>" for gitlab_issue, "<PROJECT>-<number>" for jira_issue. The character class is constrained so the LOWERCASED value is a legal item-key segment of an entry id (notably: no ':' , which is the entry-id separator).

url.description: Canonical URL of the backlog item.

entry-id.description: A stable entry id, DERIVED (never minted per run) as `<class>:<item-key>` or `<class>:<item-key>:<qualifier>` or `<class>:<key-a>+<key-b>`. Lowercase throughout, including the qualifier segment — see grooming-report-v1.md § Entry-id derivation for the normative rules, which the validator machine-checks by recomposing each id from the entry's own fields.

rubric-citation.description: One citation of a charter prioritization-rubric line justifying a score.

rubric_id.description: The charter rubric line id (e.g. "V1", "R3", "U1", "S4"). Charter ids are conventionally uppercase; entry-id qualifiers lowercase them, so charter ids must be CASE-INSENSITIVELY unique.

quote.description: Optional. The cited line's text, so a reviewer can check the citation without opening the charter.

note.description: Optional. Why this line applies to this item.

ordering-entry.description: One item's position in the proposed ranking. `rubric_citations` is REQUIRED with minItems:1 — this is the schema-level enforcement of charter §5.1 ("a score with no citation fails validation"). An entry that omits it, or ships [], is REJECTED; it is never accepted-but-undecorated.

rank.description: 1-based position in the proposed order. Ranks across the ordering array must be exactly the permutation 1..N (enforced semantically).

score.description: The groomer's numeric score. Advisory: the citations, not the number, are what the operator reviews.

rubric_citations.description: At least one charter rubric line justifying this ranking. REQUIRED and minItems:1 — the two together are the citation control.

duplicate-candidate.description: A candidate duplicate/superseded pair (charter S2). UNORDERED: the pair states that two items overlap, with no direction, which is why its id sorts the two item-keys lexicographically.

basis.description: Why the two are believed to overlap. Never destructive — a human decides.

confidence.description: The groomer's confidence in the duplication claim.

hygiene-defect.description: One objective, reversible structural defect on an item (charter S4).

defect.description: Closed set. The value is ALSO this entry's id qualifier, so one item may carry one entry per distinct defect without an id collision.

detail.description: What specifically is missing or wrong.

dependency-edge.description: A suggested dependency edge. DIRECTIONAL: `from` depends on `to`. A→B and B→A are DIFFERENT proposals with opposite meaning, so the id encodes from-key then to-key UNSORTED — a sorted derivation would collapse them onto one id, forbidding a report from proposing both directions and hiding a run-over-run edge FLIP as an unchanged id (#2240).

basis.description: Why the dependency is believed to hold.

kind.description: Edge kind. Single-value today; a future major may add blocks/relates_to.

vision-drift-flag.description: An item advancing a charter non-goal or mis-aligned with a phase theme (charter §3 / §5.3).

basis.description: Which charter surface the item drifts from.

charter_ref_id.description: The addressable charter line/theme id (e.g. "NG2", "T4"). This value is ALSO this entry's id qualifier, LOWERCASED — so charter ids must be case-insensitively unique.

detail.description: How the item drifts from the cited line.

decomposition-suggestion.description: A proposal to split one item into children. Proposal only — nothing is filed by this artifact.

rationale.description: Why the item should be split.

proposed_children.description: At least two children — a 'split' into one is not a split.
